prompt: In a sound wave traveling through air, the air molecules vibrate back and forth along the same direction the wave travels. What type of wave is this?
teacher_notes: A stretched spring demonstrates both wave types quickly.
explanation: In a longitudinal wave the oscillation of the medium is parallel to the direction of energy transfer, producing the compressions and rarefactions of a sound wave. In a transverse wave, such as a wave on a string, the medium moves perpendicular to the direction of travel. Sound requires a medium, so it is not electromagnetic.
